div.head: II Cn 71.2
div.ab: ⁊ medemra þegna: hors ⁊ his geræda ⁊ his wæpn oððe his healsfang on Wessexan; ⁊ on Myrcan II pund ⁊ on Eastenglan II pund.
Oðres ðeines. And medemra ðegen: hors ⁊ his gerædan ⁊ his wepna oððe his healsfang on Westsæxan; ⁊ on Myrcen II pund ⁊ on Eastengle II pund.
And medmera þegna: hors ⁊ his geredan ⁊ his wæpen oððe halsfange on Westsexan; ⁊ on Myrcan twa pund ⁊ on Eastengla II pund.
Et mediocris táini: equus cum apparatu suo et arma sua uel suum hálsfang in Westsexa; in Mircenis II librę; in Eastanglia II librę.
Mediocris hominis, quem Angli dicunt læsseþegen, illius heregeat est: equus et arma aut halsfang, quod est X solidi, in þeassexe; in Mercia uero et in Eastengle duę librę (denariorum).
Minoris uero uirronis: equus et apparatus eius (id est sella, frenum) et armatura eius aut collicipium illius aput Westsexam; et aput Mircen. due libre et apud Orientales Anglos due libre.
Oðres ðeines. And medemra ðegen—hors ⁊ his gerædan ⁊ his wepna oððe his healsfang on Westsæxan, ⁊ on Myrcen II pund, ⁊ on Eastengle II pund.
And medemra þegna: hors and his geræda and his wæpn oððe his healsfang on Wessexan; and on Myrcan II pund; and on Eastenglan II pund.

(Eines anderen Thegn. B) Und mittlerer Thegnas: [1] Pferd und dessen Geschirr und seine Waffen oder [statt alles dessen] seinen Halsfang [120 Schill.] in Wessex; und in Mercien 2 Pfund [120 Mercische Schill.] und in Ostanglien 2 Pfund.

(Of another thegn. B) And of lesser thegns: [1] horse and its harness and his weapons, or [instead of all that] his healsfang [120 shillings] in Wessex; and in Mercia 2 pounds [120 Mercian shillings] and in East Anglia 2 pounds.
The heriot of another thegn. And the heriot of ordinary thegns shall be a horse and its trappings and his weapons or his healsfang in Wessex, and in Mercia £2, and in East Anglia £2.
and of the lesser thegns: a horse and its trappings, and his weapons or his healsfang in Wessex; and two pounds in Mercia and two pounds in East Anglia.
And by the common thane: in Wessex, a horse and its trappings, and his weapons or his healsfang; and in Mercia, two pounds; and in East Anglia, two pounds.

Aftervassallen setzt dafür Leis Wl, ‘mediate’ verstehen Pol Mai I 293. Allein Cnut meint doch nur oder zunächst die der Krone zufliessenden Gefälle, also den Thegn (s. d. Gl 5) unmittelbar unter dem König; vgl. Wb: medeme, das nie ‘mittelbar’ bed., auch von den 3 Lateinern nicht so verstanden wird. Hier heisst es ‘nur mittelmässig’, entsprechend dem læsse maga 71, 5, der auch 2 £ zahlt. Auch der Unterschied, ob der König selbst oder [durch Pacht der Kronfinanz-Einkünfte] sein Beamter das Heergewæte (s. d. Gl 9f.) empfing, erklärt den Rang schwerlich. Letztere Einrichtung ist vielleicht erst später getroffen. In Lincolnshire erhielt ⅓ der Graf, später der Sheriff, ⅔ ein vom König privilegiertes Kloster; Domesday I 376,₂.—Inst führt den Ausdruck læsseþegen ein, wahrscheinlich—wie mehrfach bei ihm—einen echten Terminus, nicht bloss eine Kontamination aus 71, 5 und 71, 2.—Dem Heergewäte eines Mittelthegns, nicht eines Königsthegns, steht am nächsten, was in Berkshire tainus vel miles regis dominicus dem König zahlt: Waffen und 1 gesattelt, 1 ungesattelt Pferd; Domesday I 56b

Leis Wl put rear-vassals for this; Pol Mai I 293 understand ‘mediate’. But Cnut surely means only, or primarily, the dues accruing to the Crown, and hence the thegn (see that word in Gl 5) immediately under the king; cf. Wb: medeme, which never means ‘mediate’ and is not so understood by the 3 Latin translators either. Here it means ‘only middling’, corresponding to the læsse maga of 71, 5, who also pays £2. Nor does the difference whether the king himself or [through the farming of the Crown’s revenues] his official received the heriot (see that word in Gl 9f.) readily explain the rank. The latter arrangement was perhaps made only later. In Lincolnshire the earl, later the sheriff, received ⅓, and a monastery privileged by the king ⅔; Domesday I 376,₂.—Inst introduces the expression læsseþegen, probably—as several times with him—a genuine technical term, not merely a conflation of 71, 5 and 71, 2.—Closest to the heriot of a middle thegn, not of a king’s thegn, is what a tainus vel miles regis dominicus in Berkshire pays the king: arms and 1 saddled and 1 unsaddled horse; Domesday I 56b
geræðlan Fehler Thorpes; die schwache Dekl. nur aus BA bei Toller
geræðlan is Thorpe’s error; the weak declension is found in Toller only from BA
Nicht bloss Angriffswaffen [gegen Lehmann Waffen in Germania 31 (1886) 487], sondern mit Helm und Brünne; auch ahd. wafen ‘Rüstung’
Not merely offensive weapons [against Lehmann Waffen in Germania 31 (1886) 487], but including helmet and byrnie; OHG wafen too means ‘armour’

Wenn nur 1 Pferd und 1 Kriegsausrüstung im Besitze des Verstorbenen gewesen, mussten diese auf den Sohn übergehen. Vielleicht aber zog auch mancher Erbe vor, Familienstücke zu behalten und lieber Geld abzuliefern
If the deceased had possessed only 1 horse and 1 set of war-gear, these had to pass to the son. But perhaps many an heir also preferred to keep family pieces and to hand over money instead
S. Gl Halsfang 5; und zum Irrtum in Inst: 60⁸. Vielleicht ein Grosshundert Westsächs. Schillinge meint Leis Wl 20, 2
See Gl Halsfang 5; and on the error in Inst: 60⁸. Leis Wl 20, 2 perhaps means a long hundred of West Saxon shillings
Dieselbe Schillingsumme wie Halsfang des Westsächs. Thegn. Hier scheint die Zahlung in Geld obligatorisch
The same sum in shillings as the healsfang of the West Saxon thegn. Here payment in money seems to be obligatory

Da Ostanglien (s. d. Gl 7) zur Denalagu gehörte, bezweifelt Steenstrup die Originalität des Zusatzes. Allein es hatte eigenes Recht, vom Norden unterschieden, und eastinne von norðinne trennt II Ew 5, 2

Since East Anglia (see that word in Gl 7) belonged to the Danelaw, Steenstrup doubts that the addition is original. But it had a law of its own, distinct from the North, and II Ew 5, 2 distinguishes eastinne from norðinne
The reference is no doubt to medial thegns, i.e. those not under the immediate lordship of the king—the vavasours of Leis Wl. 20, 2, cf. Be Leode Geþincðum, cap. 3.
